rules.summary: The group looks like the group of a well known library
rules.explanation: A group one or two characters away from a popular one, or the same name under another top-level domain, is how typosquatting imitates a library people trust.

rules.summary: A well known artifact name is published under a foreign group
rules.explanation: The artifact carries the name of a popular library, but its group belongs to someone else. Forks do this for good reasons, impostors for bad ones.

rules.summary: The version number is unusually high
rules.explanation: Dependency confusion attacks publish an inflated version, such as 99.0.0, so that it wins conflict resolution against the real one.

rules.summary: An internal module also exists in the public repository
rules.explanation: A repository that is asked first, or one without content filtering, can serve the public module instead of yours. Declare your repository with exclusiveContent for your groups.

rules.summary: The plugin marker points to a module outside the plugin's namespace
rules.explanation: A plugin marker maps a plugin id to the module that implements it. A marker that leads to a group unrelated to the id may have been taken over.
